newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish govt in confidence vote after legal blunder.
newsitem.headline: Irish govt in confidence vote after legal blunder.

text.p: Ireland's government faced the sternest test of its two-year life on Tuesday when parliament began debating a no-confidence vote over a blunder which briefly freed 16 high-risk prisoners including suspected IRA guerrillas.

Opposition parties have called it a startling gaffe by a government pledged to curb a domestic crime wave and crack down on republican guerrilla groups who wage war against British rule of Northern Ireland.

Political sources said they expected Prime Minister John Bruton's three-party coalition government to weather the storm because of its five-seat majority but the two-day debate was expected to batter its image.

It was the first time Bruton's so-called "rainbow coalition" has faced a confidence motion since it came to power in November 1994 after the collapse of former prime minister Albert Reynolds' government in a row over legal appointments.

The opposition, led by Bertie Ahern's Fianna Fail party, has called for the resignation of Justice Minister Nora Owen over last week's blunder in which 16 prisoners were freed and had to be immediately re-arrested.
But Owen said there was no reason to resign and all three coalition parties said they would support her in the debate.
The prisoners were freed after it was discovered that the judge who detained them should no longer have been working in Ireland's three-judge anti-subversive "special criminal court".
The judge had been officially removed from the court in August, but continued to work because Owen's justice ministry forgot to inform him of the decision.

Among the prisoners involved was Nessan Quinlivan, wanted by British authorities since he escaped from London's Brixton Prison in 1991 while awaiting trial on accusations of involvement in an Irish Republican Army plot to murder British brewing tycoon Sir Charles Tidbury.
Owen said the blunder was an administrative failure and she was not directly responsible.
